content:
Can I disable this pop-up please?

Specifying the version in lakefile.toml doesn't help.
I've never seen this. Is it a windows-only thing?
It is on Windows, yes.

Martin Dvořák said:

Specifying the version in lakefile.toml doesn't help.

That's not too surprising as the Lean version goes in lean-toolchain

I'll add that it is relentlessly invasive.

I was going to ask the same question, but more to the tune of, "should I, while working on an expansive project, be on the latest Head branch and be automatically updating that according to Mathlib, or is it better to stay at a slightly lower (stable) branch and only update periodically for example at major stability points within my own project?" My own project doesn't use any of the more advanced cutting-edge sections of Mathlib, however.

Open the command palette (ctrl-shift-p) and search "open user settings" (not the json version), this gives you the UI window where you can search "update" and there is a field there for auto-updating extensions which you can set to "none" (or enabled only). There's also a field for "auto check updates" which you can turn off. I'd like to think that should kill the popup, but it is windows.. :/
Yes, it is relentlessly invasive. In just two hours, it popped up again.

If you've disabled the 'Lean 4: Always Ask Before Installing Lean Versions' setting (it's disabled by default, unless you specifically chose to enable it when installing Lean via the extension), this kind of popup only appears when you are using leanprover/lean4:stable for a Lean file somewhere. When you pick an option in the popup, it remembers it until the next time you restart VS Code.

This popup appearing likely means one of two things:

  1. You're in a project with a misconfigured lean-toolchain file that contains leanprover/lean4:stable instead of a specific Lean version. I'd strongly suggest pinning a specific Lean version in this case instead. You always want your project to explicitly declare the Lean version it should be built with.
  2. You are opening Lean files that are not in a project (e.g. untitled Lean files that do not exist on disc, or files on disc that are not in a Lean project). In this case, Lean uses the default Lean version configured in Elan, which is leanprover/lean4:stable, i.e. always the most recent stable version, by default.

The extension double-checks with users when opening such a file because both choices presented in the popup can become annoying if chosen automatically:

  1. If you are opening an untitled/project-less file to just quickly jot down some Lean code without caring too much about which specific version of Lean it is, then Elan starting an automatic installation of the newest Lean version is very annoying.
  2. If you are opening an untitled/project-less file to specifically check something on the most recent Lean version (e.g. for making an MWE), then Elan just silently reverting to whatever leanprover/lean4:stable was at when you first installed Lean (or when you last incidentally updated leanprover/lean4:stable) can be very confusing, and it may not be immediately clear to users how to fix the situation.

I suspect the problem that I hadn't anticipated when implementing this is that some users seem to constantly open untitled/project-less files without really being aware of it, so they are often faced with the popup. Clearly, this doesn't happen for Malvin, Sebastian, myself or many other users, but apparently it is a problem for users like Martin and Ian. One potential solution is to consider issue #2 as the lesser of the two evils and just silently fall back to whatever the last locally installed stable version was for untitled files, but I'm sure this will also occasionally trip people up (e.g. when producing MWEs locally).

Afaik neither (1) nor (2) is my case.
Could the problem be that I declare [[lean_lib]] through globs ?

Marc Huisinga said:

If you've disabled the 'Lean 4: Always Ask Before Installing Lean Versions' setting

Where can I check please?
Search the name of the setting in the vscode settings

Did you try my approach, Martin? I had the same issue and I tried that out (after seeing your thread), and can confirm at least on my setup, that I no longer get the popups. Ive set both of those fields to none. (I am pinned to an explicit version as well)

I am scared of editing the user settings outside of the JSON file. However, my User Settings JSON contains

"update.mode": "none",

which doesn't stop the above-mentioned behaviour.

It's the official UI though, and you can always just go right back in and change the settings. All that is going to do is force your VS code into a static mode for all extensions. You will have to keep tabs on it and do manual updates if you need them, or just put it back on auto on occasion and let it do its thing...
What is the exact name of the settings?

Its in my post above.

Extensions: Auto Check Updates

When enabled, automatically checks extensions for updates. If an extension has an update, it is marked as outdated in the Extensions view. The updates are fetched from a Microsoft online service.

Extensions: Auto Update

Controls the automatic update behavior of extensions. The updates are fetched from a Microsoft online service.
Are they settings for updates of the extension or for updates triggered by the extension?
Why not both? Not sure.. but VS code treats lean as an extension and I no longer get popups (every ten minutes about it was) when I set these to none.

Yaël Dillies said:

Search the name of the setting in the vscode settings

User Settings JSON doesn't mention lean4.alwaysAskBeforeInstallingLeanVersions at all, so I guess I have the default value, which should be OK, right?

I just restarted VS code to update some dependency graphs, and I got the popup once right at the start. I'll post here if it occurs again in this instance, but I think maybe that I'll just have the one reminder on startup (which is actually nice); the settings are still off in the UI.

Just to give another datapoint here -- I have never seen that popup in my life (I'm not on windows) and I've used lean projects with all sorts of versions of lean (eg maybe a student starts on a project using some version and never updates) so this is probably not some community-wide issue.
I see the popup on a regular basis, even when working on Mathlib. Might be a windows-specific thing.

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

I see the popup on a regular basis, even when working on Mathlib. Might be a windows-specific thing.

It would be good to know which file triggers it for you when starting VS Code.

It's not when starting VS Code. I may have been working on a file for 10 minutes, and then the popup shows up. I have just checked that Lean4: Always ask before installing Lean versions is disabled.

I'll double check everything the next time it happens to me.

Ah, oh no ... Perhaps VS Code on Windows is opening random Lean files in the background somehow that trigger the popup.

We should be able to ensure that this doesn't trigger the popup, but I also want to understand how this happens in the first place because it could also be problematic in other places (for one, depending on what file VS Code opens in the background, this may launch a language server!).
Let me set up a pre-release with some logging to see whether we can figure out what's going on.

@Sébastien Gouëzel Could you install the 0.0.238 pre-release of the extension, just use it as you normally would and then when the popup unexpectedly appears, open the developer console using the 'Developer: Toggle Developer Tools' command and look for all recent logging entries that start with Document opened, Document closed and Visible editors changed?

I hope to see some file there that you did not expect to have opened.
As a guess, perhaps this happens when looking at files in core?

Eric Wieser said:

As a guess, perhaps this happens when looking at files in core?

Oh right! I think we never ended up fixing that bug that Elan sometimes picks the wrong toolchain for files from core on Windows ...

I let my computer idle in VS code while doing kid-stuff. I haven't gotten another popup again since restarting VS-code. So one of those options definitely curtails the repetitive nature of the behavior (probably the auto check update one is enough).

Malvin Gattinger said:

Is it a windows-only thing?

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

Might be a windows-specific thing.

I see the popup a lot, on macOS. I'll screenshot it next time it happens.
@Snir Broshi Please use the pre-release above and check the developer console output.

Eric Wieser said:

As a guess, perhaps this happens when looking at files in core?

Elan 4.2.2 that fixes this behavior on Windows (and possibly macOS) has been released, please try updating and reproducing

I just got this popup on VSCodium on Linux when editing Mathlib, right after merging master onto my working copy and opening the merge editor — which I thought was expected, until I saw Always ask before installing Lean versions is disabled (but this is the default? I never touched it)
ah, actually the merge editor is editing a file under /tmp/, so perhaps this is the root cause!
but the option is disabled, and the popup appearing seems to contradict what it says

Lua Viana Reis said:

but the option is disabled, and the popup appearing seems to contradict what it says

The negation of "Always ask before installing Lean versions" is not "Never ask before installing Lean versions" :-)

Lua Viana Reis said:

ah, actually the merge editor is editing a file under /tmp/, so perhaps this is the root cause!

You're referring to the VS Code merge editor, right?

Hm, it doesn't seem to do that for me. When merging two files from a project, all documents opened by VS Code are from within that project (some get a git: URI, but we deliberately ignore those in the extension).
This editor is opened when I do jj resolve, which creates these files for 3-way merge in /tmp. It's kinda pointless to start a LSP server there, so it would be nice if the extension did not...
What if you have a genuine standalone file in /tmp that you want to look at in your editor? (E.g. AI agents love to create files there as well)
perhaps an option to blacklist specific paths like /tmp/jj-resolve-*?
(VisualJJ also seems to do the right thing here - it tags the diff file with a different URI schema, like the Git integration does as well)
I mostly use the command line with jj... I wonder if git in the command line would create files in there as well?

Git also opens them in the folder, as it should:

+1 for visualjj :) . That /tmp behavior seems potentially problematic for many other language servers/editor tools as well
Maybe we should add an option to disable LSP for Lean files not in a project, so that VSCode become a pure text editor (with basic Lean syntax highlighting).
